mechanism_narrative: A persistent rebound in WORKPLACES mobility after a near-flat week signals more commuting and lunch-hour trips, which lifts RETAIL_REC within four weeks because weekday shopping is pulled by office presence.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -10.0 to around 0 before dropping back to -9.9, while TRANSIT stayed near -5 to -7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not improve together over the next four weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises, the commuting-to-retail mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while TRANSIT stays suppressed, more trips are consolidated into home-centered behavior and discretionary retail is displaced, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -7 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +6
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 6.1 to 7.7 while TRANSIT is -8.7 to -5.4 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -7 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +6 but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days, the home-substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in PARKS mobility above its recent trough indicates stronger outdoor leisure demand, and that spillover supports adjacent retail and dining visits within one week, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rebounds by at least 4 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -21.9 at t-2w and then stayed around -17.6
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by at least 4 points from one week to the next and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the spillover claim is false.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in WORKPLACES combined with weaker TRANSIT indicates a tightening mobility regime that suppresses nonessential shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops below -5 while TRANSIT is below -7 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -9.9 and TRANSIT is -7.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -5 and TRANSIT stays below -7 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 28 days, the restriction-suppression mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A stable gap where GROCERY_PHARM stays far above baseline while RETAIL_REC stays below baseline reflects substitution toward essential purchasing, which keeps discretionary retail weak over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is above +41 throughout while RETAIL_REC remains near -9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above +40 and RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises over the next 14 days, the essential-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated, warm-weather or holiday-style local leisure concentrates time locally and diverts trips from shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC weakens over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stays negative but less volatile while RESIDENTIAL stays above +6
failure_condition: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL remain elevated but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the local-leisure diversion hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week rise in TRANSIT from a depressed level increases incidental exposure to shopping corridors, and that impulse traffic lifts RETAIL_REC with a short lag of one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points week-on-week from a negative level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -8.7 to -5.4 before slipping back to -7.4
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points from one week to the next and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the transit-exposure mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES contracts while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, it indicates a work-from-home regime that reduces weekday retail trips; RETAIL_REC should fall relative to the prior four weeks over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns negative again after being near zero and RESIDENTIAL stays above +6
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -0.3 and -0.1 before dropping to -9.9; RESIDENTIAL stays 6.1 to 7.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays negative while RESIDENTIAL stays above +6 yet RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days, the work-from-home suppression hypothesis fails.
